content.text:
I submitted **index 14** (Sb 0.24 / Y 0.76) as the best composition, but its EQE is only 2.7×10⁻⁴ %. This Sb–Y oxide library responds almost not at all to 2.7 eV light, so the result says little about where a real optimum would be.

I used all three merit measurements:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 28 | 0.67 | 1.4×10⁻⁴ |
| **14** | **0.24** | **2.7×10⁻⁴** |
| 9 | 0.14 | −8×10⁻⁵ (effectively zero) |

- **Why the signal is so weak:** the model predicts the Y-containing phases can't absorb 2.7 eV photons. Predicted band gaps are 5.6 eV for Y₂O₃, 3.6 eV for Y₃SbO₇ and 3.4 eV for Sb₅Y₃O₁₂. Only the antimony oxide Sb₆O₁₃ (predicted 2.05 eV) should absorb at 2.7 eV. The model gave Y₂Sb₂O₇ a 0.1 eV gap, which I treated as an error, since that crystal type is normally an insulator.
- **How I chose the samples:** I measured the Sb-rich end first, expecting Sb₆O₁₃ to help, but it gave almost nothing. Then I measured the middle of the line, then index 9 on the Y-rich side, which the fitted model suggested.
- **What's uncertain:** with three points on a 29-sample line, a better composition I didn't sample could exist, most likely between Sb 0.14 and 0.35. I didn't use any of the five XRD measurements, so I haven't confirmed which crystal phases are actually present at index 14.
